meta.title: Hive: browser task → CLI worker → team

components.label: Browser workbench
components.explanation: The user types into the orchestrator terminal. The terminal client sends input on its IO socket and renders returning output after restoring the terminal snapshot. Separately, report notifications poll committed dispatches every two seconds; the Action Center polls summaries. Editing a task-list checkbox is not itself a worker dispatch.

components.label: Terminal stream hub
components.explanation: The local WebSocket server validates the UI session and run ID before attaching IO/control channels at /ws/terminal/:runId/{io,control}. The hub writes browser input through store.writeRunInput. Agent PTY onData publishes to the output bus; subscribed viewers receive live output. Both orchestrator and worker are terminal runs, not browser-hosted agent code.

components.label: Orchestrator CLI
components.explanation: A CLI agent receives the user's terminal input and decides whether and how to delegate. Its team send subcommand POSTs the member name, task text, workspace ID, agent ID and token to the loopback runtime. Status and report text are subsequently injected back into this CLI's stdin. The external agent's reasoning, tool execution and adherence to prompts cannot be established from Hive source.

components.label: Team protocol + dispatch
components.explanation: Authenticated workspace-scoped Team routes resolve the worker and create a queued or submitted dispatch. The stdin dispatcher formats prompts, serializes writes per agent and waits for startup readiness. Task-scoped team message --kind progress is stored without model delivery or advancing the required input sequence; it remains visible to UI/CLI reads. Legacy team status logs and forwards into orchestrator stdin without closing work. Reports settle the matching open responsibility and enqueue a durable return payload atomically; outbox delivery is acknowledged only after the PTY write resolves.

components.label: Worker CLI
components.explanation: AgentManager uses node-pty to launch the configured CLI and writes to its process input. The environment includes HIVE_PROJECT_ID, HIVE_AGENT_ID, HIVE_PORT and HIVE_AGENT_TOKEN; the packaged team command is prepended to PATH. The worker can call team message --dispatch D --to orchestrator --kind progress for silent task-scoped updates, legacy team status for injected updates, and team report for explicit completion with optional artifact paths. Raw terminal output does not itself settle a responsibility.

components.label: Local SQLite state
components.explanation: Runtime services wire the dispatch ledger, message log and report outbox into Team operations, using a database transaction for protocol writes. Completion requires a matching open dispatch and seen_seq equal to the latest required inbound message sequence; otherwise it is rejected with 409. A committed report is distinct from successful delivery into the orchestrator's terminal.

sources.label: Progress stored, not queued to model

cards.title: Dispatch is explicit
items: The orchestrator calls team send; the task-list editor does not launch a worker.
Stopped user-managed workers keep queued work until restarted. Only a never-started orchestrator-spawned worker auto-starts on team send.

cards.title: Progress ≠ completion
items: Task-scoped progress is stored for UI/CLI reads, not injected into a model. Legacy team status is injected; neither closes work. Raw terminal output streams separately.
team report requires the open dispatch and exact inbound seen_seq. The report, ledger change and outbox commit together.

cards.title: Return and scope
items: Reports survive an unavailable orchestrator in the outbox; team list drains them after restart. Status forwarding has no equivalent report-outbox retry.

Task-list file sync is separate: .hive/tasks.md → watcher → /ws/tasks. Agent reasoning and actual task success are external, not proven by a PTY write. Remote tunnels and experimental workflows are outside this local path.
